listing_view.reasoning: Demand is weak: the book was only ~0.86x subscribed two days in with no acceleration in the final readings, and there is no grey-market, anchor, or broker data to suggest a pop is being underwritten. To be wrong, there would need to be a late-day institutional surge on day three that simply isn't visible in the recorded history.

longterm_view.reasoning: Reported profits look healthy on paper (PAT margins 18-25%), but the cash tells the opposite story: operating cash flow was negative in two of three years and latest-year cash conversion is deeply negative, while receivable days exploded from 35 to 137. Returns on capital and equity are both declining, so the 'quality' the P&L implies is not being realised as cash.

governance.reasoning: The company has an open SEBI Show Cause Notice, a paid SEBI penalty of Rs 4 lakh, and a separate show cause notice in its capacity as a registered Investment Adviser [litigation, page 608], [litigation, page 610]. None of this is disqualifying, but a regulated financial-business issuer arriving at IPO with live SEBI process is a negative, not a neutral.

key_risks.why_it_matters: Payment terms stretched from 35 to 137 days in two years, which is the classic signature of revenue being booked faster than cash is collected, and the extracts contain no explanation or customer breakdown.
Operating cash flow was negative in two of the three reported years despite large reported EBITDA, so the earnings quality underpinning the ask is unproven.
An open SEBI show cause notice against the company and its role as a SEBI-registered Investment Adviser means adverse action could hit both valuation and licence to operate.
Revenue fell 24% in the latest year and both ROCE and ROE are falling, so the IPO is being sold off a shrinking, lower-returning base.
